text:
maria: Heads up — running into a weird pattern with the Go SSE client where partial JSON boundaries + token refreshes cause a sudden backlog and CPU spike. Repro locally with a small harness that splits frames mid-object.

maria: Minimal repro (pseudo):
```go
buf := make([]byte, 0)
for {
  n, _ := conn.Read(tmp)
  buf = append(buf, tmp[:n]...)
  // naive: try decode full object each iteration
  var obj map[string]interface{}
  if err := json.Unmarshal(buf, &obj); err == nil {
    process(obj)
    buf = buf[:0]
  }
}
```

maria: When a large stream with many small events hits and chunks split in the middle of strings/braces, the loop re-triggers lots of goroutines which then block on our outbound queue — bursty backlog.

kai: Are you using json.Decoder or raw Unmarshal? Decoder can handle streams if you loop with Decoder.More()/Decode. But that still assumes full object boundaries are present.

sam: Two orthogonal fixes: 1) make the parser incremental/stateful (so partial tokens don't cause full Unmarshal attempts), 2) add backpressure on read path (limit bytes buffered per-connection and block upstream). We do both on other SDKs.

arjun: For Go specifically, json.Decoder is better; also look at decoder.Buffered() to get leftover bytes after a Decode attempt. Example pattern: create decoder := json.NewDecoder(reader); for decoder.More() { var ev Event; if err := decoder.Decode(&ev); ... }

jen: If the stream is NDJSON you can ReadBytes('\n') from a bufio.Reader, but server isn't NDJSON here — it's chunked SSE with json objects inside data:. So we can't rely on newline delimiting.

maria: Right — server emits SSE data chunks like `data: {"..."}\n\n` and some clients see the packet split such that we get `data: {"par` then next read `tial":...}`.

kai: Two practical client changes that helped us in similar infra: 1) switch to a small incremental json tokenizer (eg github.com/json-iterator/go or a tiny state machine) that can return when it has a full top-level value, 2) implement a bounded in-memory buffer per connection (e.g., 256KB) and apply a backpressure signal (block the SSE reader goroutine or return an error upstream to the reconnect/backoff layer) once exceeded.

sam: For backpressure implementation in Go, simplest is a semaphore channel:
```go
var bytesInFlight = make(chan struct{}, maxBytes) // not literal bytes but units
// read loop
if len(bytesInFlight)+len(buf) > threshold { // block until some released
  <-bytesInFlight
}
bytesInFlight <- struct{}{}
// process, then release
<-bytesInFlight
```
This pattern avoids unbounded memory and surfaces load to the caller. Use real token-bucket (x/time/rate) if you want smoothing.

arjun: Also add a small jittered sleep before spawning processors when backlog is high — reduces thundering herd.

maria: I tried a quick change using json.Decoder but still saw hangs when partial multibyte UTF-8 splits happen (decoder complained about invalid UTF-8). That suggests we need to accumulate bytes until we have a valid UTF-8 sequence before handing to decoder.

jen: Good catch — need to ensure you don't split inside a rune. Use utf8.FullRune on the buffered tail: if !utf8.FullRune(tail) { wait for more bytes }

maria: Logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z read 128 bytes: "...\u00f"
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z json: invalid UTF-8
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z goroutines: 512 backlog: 48 queued_msgs
```

kai: For a long-term fix: 1) stateful incremental parser (handle partial runes), 2) apply per-conn backpressure + metrics. Short-term: clamp buffer size and return an error to trigger client reconnect which is cheaper than OOM/goroutine explosion.

maria: I'll open a PR with: incremental UTF-8 safe accumulator, json.Decoder loop guarded by utf8.FullRune on tails, and a simple rate limiter (x/time/rate) that throttles spawn of processors. Also add an integration test that splits objects at rune boundaries and at brace boundaries.

ci-bot: CI: Created pipeline for branch fix/sse-reassembly-maria. Tests queued.

sam: Ping me for a quick review — I can help with the rate-limiter bits and integration harness.

arjun: If you want I can sketch a small state machine for top-level object detection (count braces while tracking strings/escapes) — it's tiny and avoids general parser dep.

maria: Thanks — assigning: I'll draft PR today, include tests + perf run, tag @sam and @arjun for review.

jen: Thanks, will add a dashboard tile for sse.buffered_bytes and sse.goroutine_count so we can catch regressions. :thumbsup:

maria: Awesome — will link the PR here when ready.
